rows.original: You step through the wood-paneled door and into a round room all done in even more fake wood paneling, making it look like you’re surrounded by dozens of tree trunks. The upper parts of the walls are painted to look like treetops, complete with patches of blue sky peeking through, and the entire place feels like you’ve stepped out of Tavros Station and right into a forest. The illusion is broken by a tall silver machine standing in the center of the room, with a large monitor on one side and some kind of scanning device sticking out of the top. A padded reclining chair stands to one side of the machine, made for someone to sit down and get comfortable, while a flat table that’s large enough to hold most people stands on the other side. A door marked ‘Staff Only’ stands closed in the middle of a tree trunk to the left. The wall to the right lacks the wood paneling, instead holding a bunch of monitors showing all different kinds of tattoos. A counter stands in front of the wall of monitors, and a woman stands behind it, next to a simple tablet workstation. The woman looks human at first glance, but the round, brown-furred ears sticking up out of her mass of curly blue hair show she has some mixed heritage, as does the darkness around her eyes that fades outward to match her tan skin. She’s dressed very casually, with an open-sided shirt and black sports bra over her sizable chest, and both her shoulders are tattooed. The woman gives you a bright smile, and steps out from behind the counter. “Hey, what’s up? I’m Catalina, and this is Treetop Tattoos.” She seems very informal, but you suppose getting a tattoo isn’t exactly like making a business deal. “What’s your name?” You tell her your name, and if she recognizes your last name, she doesn’t show it. And now that she’s not behind the counter, you can see that Catalina’s wearing tight athletic shorts over some strong legs; it looks like she spends plenty of time working out or used to be some kind of athlete. More tattoos, black leopard spots, rise up over both her hips. And that’s not all you can see – the woman’s packing a bulge at the front, with two sizable balls. She seems very casual about just having it out there. “Good to meet you,” Catalina says, still smiling. “So, like you probably guessed, we do tattoos here. I can ink mostly anything on mostly anyone, and it’s all done with some pretty basic microsurgeons, so there’s no worry about infection, and it’s easy to fix up or remove if you change your mind.” She shoots you a grin. “I got to get that out there right away, so many people come in here thinking it’s a lifetime thing when it’s like, no, you can get inked up for a weekend or a night out and then get it all taken out before you’ve got to go back to work.” Good to know. You tell her you’ve never had a nanotech tattoo before, and her brown eyes light up. “You picked a great place to start.” Catalina steps back behind her counter, and taps on her tablet. The monitors behind her swap to line drawings on a white background, displaying all kinds of art, ranging from spaceships to abstracts to things you’d see on a poster in a red light district. “This is most of what I do,” she says. “I get lots of people here who want something badass or something sexy, or a special picture for a special thing.” She picks up a stylus from the counter, and twirls it between her fingers, the movements quick and deft. “But I can draw just about anything you want, and we’ll scan you and get a pic to see what it looks like before the ink drops. What d’you think?”
rows.translation: 你穿过木质镶板门，进入一间圆形房间，四周铺着更多仿木镶板，看起来就像被几十根树干环绕。墙壁上半部画成树冠模样，还留出几片蓝天从枝叶间露出，整间店让你感觉自己一步离开塔夫罗斯空间站，直接踏进森林。 这份幻觉被房间中央一台高大的银色机器打破。它一侧装着大型显示器，顶部伸出某种扫描装置。机器旁边放着一张带软垫的躺椅，供人坐下放松；另一侧则是一张足以承载大多数人的平桌。左边一根树干中央有扇标着“员工专用”的门，紧紧关闭。右侧墙壁没有仿木镶板，取而代之的是许多显示不同纹身的屏幕。 屏幕墙前摆着柜台，一个女人站在柜台后，身旁是一套简易平板工作台。乍看之下她像是人类，但一头蓬松卷曲的蓝发间伸出的棕色圆耳显示她拥有混血血统；眼睛周围的深色区域向外渐淡，最终与棕褐肤色融为一体，也说明了这一点。她穿得非常休闲，敞开两侧的上衣和黑色运动胸罩包裹着丰满胸部，两边肩膀上都有纹身。 女人朝你灿烂一笑，从柜台后走出来。“嘿，怎么样？我是卡塔利娜，这里是树顶纹身店。”她显得非常随意，不过你想，纹身确实不像洽谈商业交易。“你叫什么名字？” 你告诉她自己的名字；即使她认出了你的姓氏，也没有表现出来。现在她不再站在柜台后，你能看见卡塔利娜穿着紧身运动短裤，包裹着结实双腿；看起来她经常锻炼，或者曾经是某种运动员。更多黑色豹斑纹身沿两侧臀部向上延伸。而你看见的还不止这些：这个女人裤裆前鼓起一包，还带着两颗相当大的睾丸。她似乎完全不介意就这样把它们显露出来。 “很高兴认识你，”卡塔利娜依然笑着说道。“所以，就像你大概已经猜到的，我们这里做纹身。我几乎能在任何人身上纹任何图案，而且全程只用相当基础的微型外科机器人，所以不用担心感染；如果你改变主意，也很容易修补或移除。”她朝你咧嘴一笑。“我得立刻把这件事说清楚，因为太多人走进来时都以为纹身是一辈子的事；其实根本不是，你完全可以为了周末或者夜间外出纹满全身，然后在回去工作以前全部移除。” 很有用的信息。你告诉她自己以前从没做过纳米科技纹身，她的棕色双眼顿时亮了起来。 “你的入门地点选得很棒。”卡塔利娜回到柜台后，在平板上轻点。身后的屏幕切换成白色背景上的线稿，展示各种各样的图案，从宇宙飞船到抽象艺术，再到红灯区海报上会出现的东西，应有尽有。“我主要做的就是这些，”她说道。“很多人来这里，是想要凶悍一点、性感一点的东西，或者为某件特别的事准备一幅特别的图案。”她从柜台拿起一支触控笔，在指间快速灵巧地转动。“不过你想要的东西，我几乎都能画。我们还会扫描你的身体，做出预览图，让你在落墨前看看效果。你觉得怎么样？”

rows.original: You ask Catalina to tell you about the shop, as she’s clearly put a lot into it. “It’s pretty fucking cool, isn’t it?” she says, then spreads her arms, gesturing to the entire place. When you don’t say anything, she lets her arms drop, and shrugs. “Okay, it’s gonna be great someday, I’m just getting started. I figure once people start learning about the place, it’ll become a Tavros mainstay, and then I’ll be set.” She’s definitely in the right place for it. With all the travelers and Rushers coming through, there are bound to be plenty of people who want to get inked. “That’s the hope, [pc.name],” Catalina says. “I wanted to make it stand out, y’know, really catch some eyes as people walk through this place. That’s why I went with the treetop thing, because nobody thinks they’re gonna find a forest when they’re on a space station.” She leans one hip against the counter again, and looks up at the painted trees, a calmer expression on her face. “That’s not the only reason why, though. I mean, it works for this place, but I think any shop I opened up would have looked like this. The forest’s special to me, that’s why I got this ink.” She turns and shows you a tree of life on her right shoulder, done all in dark green. “Ever been to Jitafore?” You can’t say that you have, unless it was so long ago that you don’t remember. “It’s amazing,” Catalina says, and starts to grin. “It’s my kui-tan mom’s home world, so we headed there like once a year when I was growing up, to see the family and stuff like that. So much forest, just going on and on forever. I remember the first time I went there, I was maybe six, and it was like I could just get lost in the forests, because everything was so damn big.” She pauses, and narrows her eyes a little. “Though a bunch of the kids there called me stub-tail because my tail’s so short, but they can fuck off. Damn kids.” So that’s why she went with the forest theme for the shop? It must have taken some time to find someone to paint the place like this. “Not so long as you’d think,” she says, giving you a considering look. “I started making connections, like, right away once I decided to start up here. Finding artists took a little while, but I had credits and big damn walls, so it wasn’t too hard to find someone who could do some good forests.” She shrugs. “But yeah, I wanted to make a place that reminded me of that moon. It’s been way too long since I went back.” That’s too bad. And she’s kind of stuck here running the shop now, isn’t she? “Not forever,” Catalina says, a determined look on her face. She stands up a little straighter, instead of leaning against the counter. “I’ve got plans for this place. Step one, get myself established. Shouldn’t be too hard, like I said, since there’s a ton of people running through this station and I’m the only one doing ink.” She holds up her hand, curls out one finger, then a second. “Step two, get big enough to turn the place into a real house of ink, so it’s not just me working here.” She gestures to the wall opposite her. “I checked into it, and there’s room to expand. So if I make enough credits and find some other reliable inkers, I can make this forest grow.” And step three? Catalina smirks as she holds up a third finger. “Step three is always the same: profit!” She cackles, then gets serious again all at once. “But seriously, making a bunch of credits with this place is the major goal. I’m not thinking franchises, but give me a few years and I bet I can have tattoo fans from all over space coming here to get inked, not just people passing through. Once I’ve got a set and steady customer base and I’m reeling in the credits, I can move to step four.” So she’s made plans beyond profit? That’s more than some business plans you’ve seen. “Of course,” Catalina says, then huffs out a breath. “Whole point of working a lot right now is so I can make tons of credits and not have to work when I’m older. Once I’ve got this place rolling in, I’ll sell it. Maybe to whoever’s working here and wants to keep it going, maybe to some company who wants to buy it, who knows. Whatever gets me enough credits to head out and see a bunch of new worlds and make art for myself while I’m there. That’s the dream,” she adds, holding out a fourth finger. That’s quite the goal. And she’ll need a lot of credits to travel the galaxy. You carefully don’t mention that you personally know how much it all costs thanks to how you were brought up, but there’s no point in not telling her the obvious. “I know, I know,” she says, and rolls her eyes. “Both my moms are in finance, they got me the loan for this place. Mostly because we’ve heard horror stories about the people who do loans here on the station.” She shivers a little, though it looks like she’s being dramatic. “But yeah, I grew up with stock reports for bedtime stories. Maybe I’ll never be rich, but I can make this work for the life I want.” It sounds like a good goal, so long as she’s realistic about it. And if this place takes off, she could get there sooner than she thinks. “That’s the goal.” Catalina looks around the small studio, a wistful expression on her tanned face. “I mean, I’m a lot more about the art than the business stuff. My moms made me learn finance because they knew it’d make life easier for me. But having enough creds to not even need the business anymore, and just go travel and draw? That’s the life, [pc.name]. That’s the fucking best life.” It’s a good dream. And with the Planet Rush going on, there’ll be new places to go once she’s able to travel. “Ooh, I know,” she says, excitement shining in her eyes. “I’ve had some Rushers come through, and they told me about the places they’ve been to. Some of those new worlds sound so cool! I can’t wait to get out there, even if it’s gonna be years until then.”
rows.translation: 你请卡塔利娜介绍一下店铺，因为她显然投入了许多心血。 “这里他妈很酷，对吧？”她说着张开双臂，朝整个店铺示意。你没有说话，她便放下双臂，耸了耸肩。“好吧，总有一天会变得很棒，我才刚刚起步。我想，等大家开始知道这个地方，它就会成为塔弗罗斯的老字号，到时我就稳了。” 她确实选对了地方。这么多旅行者和大淘金者来来往往，肯定有许多人想纹身。 “希望如此，[pc.name]，”卡塔利娜说道。“我想让这里显眼一点，你知道的，让人们走过这里时真正注意到它。所以我选择了树冠主题，因为身处空间站时，没人会想到自己竟然能发现一片森林。” 她再次让一侧髋部倚着柜台，抬头望向彩绘树木，表情变得更加平静。“但这不是唯一的原因。我的意思是，这主题确实适合这里，不过我想，无论开哪家店，我大概都会把它装饰成这个样子。森林对我而言意义非凡，所以我才纹了这个。”她转过身，向你展示右肩上一棵完全以深绿色绘成的生命之树。“你去过吉塔福尔吗？” 你不能说自己去过，除非那是久远到已经忘记的事情。 “那里美极了，”卡塔利娜咧嘴笑道。“那是我奎坦妈妈的母星，所以小时候我们差不多每年都会去一次，探望家人什么的。到处都是森林，无边无际地一直延伸。我记得第一次去时大概六岁，感觉自己随时都能迷失在森林里，因为所有东西都他妈那么巨大。”她顿了顿，微微眯起双眼。“不过，那里的许多孩子因为我的尾巴太短，叫我短尾巴；但他们都滚一边去吧。该死的小鬼。” 所以，她正因如此才给店铺选择了森林主题？要找到能把这里画成这样的人，肯定花了不少时间。 “没有你想象中那么久，”她说着，若有所思地看了你一眼。“决定在这里创业后，我几乎立刻开始建立人脉。寻找艺术家确实花了一点时间，但我有信用点，也有一大片该死的墙壁，所以找到能画出漂亮森林的人并不太难。”她耸耸肩。“不过没错，我想创造一个能让我想起那颗卫星的地方。我已经太久没回去了。” 那真遗憾。而且她现在有点被困在这里经营店铺了，对吧？ “不会永远这样，”卡塔利娜说道，神情坚定。她不再倚着柜台，而是把身体站得更直。“我替这里制定了计划。第一步，站稳脚跟。就像我说的，应该不会太难；毕竟有这么多人经过空间站，而我是唯一做纹身的人。” 她举起手，先伸出一根手指，接着又伸出第二根。“第二步，把规模扩大到足以让这里成为真正的纹身殿堂，不再只有我一个人工作。”她朝对面的墙壁示意。“我调查过，有扩建空间。所以只要赚到足够的信用点，再找到一些可靠的纹身师，我就能让这片森林继续生长。” 第三步呢？ 卡塔利娜伸出第三根手指，得意地笑了。“第三步永远都一样：赚钱！”她咯咯大笑，随后又突然严肃起来。“不过说真的，靠这个地方赚取大量信用点才是主要目标。我没打算开连锁店，但给我几年时间，我敢说能让来自宇宙各处的纹身爱好者专程到这里纹身，而不只是接待路过的人。一旦拥有一批固定而稳定的客户，开始大把赚取信用点，我就可以进入第四步。” 所以，她连赚钱之后的计划都做好了？这已经胜过你见过的一些商业计划。 “当然，”卡塔利娜说完呼出一口气。“现在拼命工作的全部意义，就是让我赚到大量信用点，年纪大了以后不必再工作。等这里开始财源滚滚，我就把店卖掉。也许卖给在这里工作、想继续经营的人，也许卖给某家想收购它的公司，谁知道呢。只要能让我拿到足够的信用点，然后出发去看看一大堆新世界，并在那里为自己创作艺术，怎样都行。那就是梦想，”她又补充道，同时伸出第四根手指。 这目标相当远大。她需要许多信用点才能遨游银河。你谨慎地没有提起，凭借自己的成长经历，你亲自知道这一切有多么昂贵；不过，显而易见的事实也没有必要不告诉她。 “我知道，我知道，”她说着翻了个白眼。“我的两位妈妈都从事金融，是她们替我弄到了这家店的贷款。主要因为我们听过不少恐怖故事，内容都与空间站里放贷的人有关。”她略微颤抖了一下，不过看起来只是故意夸张。“不过没错，我从小听着股票报告当睡前故事长大。也许我永远成不了富人，但可以让这个计划支撑自己想要的生活。” 只要她保持现实，这就是个好目标。如果这家店生意起飞，她甚至可能比想象中更早实现梦想。 “这就是目标。”卡塔利娜环顾小小的工作室，小麦色脸庞上带着憧憬。“我的意思是，比起商业上的东西，我更加重视艺术。妈妈们逼我学习金融，因为她们知道这会让我生活得更轻松。不过，要是能拥有多到不再需要做生意的信用点，只管旅行和画画？那才叫生活，[pc.name]。那他妈才是最棒的生活。” 这是个好梦想。而且星球大淘金正在进行；等她有能力旅行时，又会出现新的去处。 “噢，我知道，”她说道，双眼闪耀着兴奋。“有些大淘金者来过这里，给我讲了他们去过的地方。某些新世界听起来酷极了！我等不及想亲自出去看看，哪怕那还得再等许多年。”

rows.raw: "The Rush"

rows.original: She definitely sounds excited about traveling. Maybe once you’ve been to a Rush planet or two, you could tell her about some of your travels.

rows.translation: 大淘金
rows.raw: "The Rush"

rows.original: You tell Catalina that you’re on Tavros because of the Planet Rush, and you’re out to see as much as you can. You kind of talk around the real reason you’re doing this, but her eyes go wide when you bring it up, and she leans forward as soon as you finish talking. “Tell me everything,” she says, clearly more than a little eager.
rows.translation: 你告诉卡塔利娜，自己来到塔弗罗斯是为了参加星球大淘金，打算尽可能多地见识外面的世界。你含糊带过了真正这么做的原因，但当你提起大淘金时，她的双眼顿时睁大；你刚说完，她便向前倾身。 “全都讲给我听，”她说道，显然急切得不得了。
rows.raw: "You tell Catalina that you’re on Tavros because of the Planet Rush, and you’re out to see as much as you can. You kind of talk around the real reason you’re doing this, but her eyes go wide when you bring it up, and she leans forward as soon as you finish talking.\n\n\t\t“Tell me everything,” she says, clearly more than a little eager. "

rows.original: You tell her about the first planet you went to, the jungle world of Mhen’ga, home to insect people and strange flying membranes and a species that seemed to be all women with tentacles for skirts. Catalina looks at you a little strangely at that one, but she nods, taking it all in. “Sounds like a hell of a place,” she says. “The forest’s like home to me, but jungles where you can’t see, like, ten feet away? That would creep me the hell out. Especially if there’s bug people hiding around there.” She shudders. “I’m fine with insects so long as they’re small. Giant ones that could talk? Nope. Just nope.” The zil look humanoid enough, but maybe that wouldn’t change things for her.
rows.translation: 你告诉她，自己去的第一颗星球是丛林世界门加，那里住着昆虫人，有奇怪的飞行膜翼，还有一种似乎全是女性、用触手充当裙子的种族。听到最后一种时，卡塔利娜古怪地看了你一眼，不过仍点点头，把一切听进耳中。 “听起来真是个不得了的地方，”她说。“森林对我来说就像家一样，但那种，呃，十英尺外都看不清的丛林？绝对会把我吓坏。尤其里面还藏着昆虫人。”她打了个寒颤。“昆虫只要够小，我完全没意见。能开口说话的巨型昆虫？不行，绝对不行。” 兹尔人的外形已经很接近人类，不过这或许也不会改变她的看法。

rows.translation: 你继续讲述门加之旅，说自己如何深入丛林，直到看够了那地方的一切，随后前往下一站。
rows.raw: "You continue your tale of Mhen’ga, talking about how you delved into the jungle until you’d seen enough of the place, and moved on to your next stop. "

rows.original: You tell her that you’re still exploring Mhen’ga, but you’ll probably see all you want to see and move on soon.
rows.translation: 你告诉她，自己仍在探索门加，不过大概很快就会看尽想看的东西，然后继续前进。
rows.raw: "You tell her that you’re still exploring Mhen’ga, but you’ll probably see all you want to see and move on soon. "

rows.original: “Where’d you go next?” Catalina asks. You tell her about Tarkus, two planets bolted together by the natives. Her eyes almost pop out of her head when she hears that, and she starts scribbling down sketches on her tablet as you talk, like she’s trying to capture the concept as quickly as you tell her about it. She keeps sketching as you talk about the place’s mechanically-inclined natives and the endless fields of rust. “That is seriously fucking wild,” she says, her ears tilting forward as she focuses on her art. After a moment or two, she puts her stylus down, and gives you a smile. “Sorry, I just had to get that down, I’ll make it better later. I had no idea there was a world like that out there.”
rows.translation: “下一站去哪了？”卡塔利娜问道。 你向她讲起塔卡斯，那是两颗被当地人铆接到一起的星球。听到这里，她的眼珠子都快瞪出来了；你讲话时，她开始在平板上飞快勾画草图，似乎想以和你讲述同样快的速度捕捉这个概念。你谈起当地擅长机械的原住民与一望无际的锈蚀荒野时，她仍在不断绘画。 “这也太他妈离谱了，”她说，专注于画作时双耳朝前倾斜。过了一会儿，她放下触控笔，对你微微一笑。“抱歉，我就是非得先把它记下来，之后再画得更好。我完全不知道外面还有这样的世界。”
rows.raw: "“Where’d you go next?” Catalina asks. You tell her about Tarkus, two planets bolted together by the natives. Her eyes almost pop out of her head when she hears that, and she starts scribbling down sketches on her tablet as you talk, like she’s trying to capture the concept as quickly as you tell her about it. She keeps sketching as you talk about the place’s mechanically-inclined natives and the endless fields of rust. “That is seriously fucking wild,” she says, her ears tilting forward as she focuses on her art. After a moment or two, she puts her stylus down, and gives you a smile. “Sorry, I just had to get that down, I’ll make it better later. I had no idea there was a world like that out there.”"

rows.original: That’s not even the weirdest part. You tell her about the tether that holds the two halves of the world together, and how you actually journeyed to it before heading off to your next destination.
rows.translation: 这甚至还不是最古怪的部分。你告诉她，世界两半之间由一条系链维系；而在前往下一处目的地之前，你还亲自去过那里。
rows.raw: "\n\nThat’s not even the weirdest part. You tell her about the tether that holds the two halves of the world together, and how you actually journeyed to it before heading off to your next destination. "

rows.original: You tell her that you’re still exploring Tarkus, and you’re sure there’s still plenty of it to see before you move on.
rows.translation: 你告诉她，自己仍在探索塔卡斯；继续前进之前，那里肯定还有许多地方可看。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou tell her that you’re still exploring Tarkus, and you’re sure there’s still plenty of it to see before you move on. "

rows.original: “I dunno if you can top two half-planets chained together,” Catalina says, “but where’d you go next?” You tell her about Myrellion, which felt very different from the first two planets you visited, even if their tech was millennia behind. Catalina starts to frown upon hearing about the two warring groups of people, and shakes her head as you tell her some details about their ongoing conflict. “That’s just sad,” she says with a sigh. “I know we’re gonna find all kinds of weird things in the Planet Rush – I read about some of the other ones, back in my history classes. But it’s like, we keep seeing the same kinds of conflicts over and over no matter where we go.” She pauses. “But I mean, if I’ve got to go to war, I’ll go on the side that has the women with their boobs constantly swelling up, know what I mean?” Somehow, she grins despite how serious she was a moment ago.
rows.translation: “两颗被锁链拴在一起的半星球，我不知道你还能不能超越这个，”卡塔利娜说道，“不过下一站是哪？” 你向她讲起米瑞利恩。尽管当地科技落后了数千年，但那颗星球给人的感觉与前两颗大不相同。听说那里有两群人正在交战后，卡塔利娜皱起眉头；当你讲述这场持续冲突的部分细节时，她摇了摇头。 “真可悲，”她叹息道。“我知道我们会在星球大淘金中发现各种怪事——以前上历史课时，我读过其他几次大淘金的资料。但无论我们去哪里，似乎总会一遍遍看到同一种冲突。”她顿了顿。“不过我的意思是，如果非要参战，我肯定会加入那些女人乳房一直在膨胀的一方，懂吧？”尽管片刻前还那么严肃，她不知怎么又咧嘴笑了。

Catalina starts to frown upon hearing about the two warring groups of people, and shakes her head as you tell her some details about their ongoing conflict. “That’s just sad,” she says with a sigh. “I know we’re gonna find all kinds of weird things in the Planet Rush – I read about some of the other ones, back in my history classes. rows.original: There’s even more to the planet than that. You tell Catalina about your adventures delving into the depths of Myrellion, and finding yet another group of people down there, even meeting the one they called their queen. She just shakes her head, like she can hardly believe some of the stuff you’re telling her.
rows.translation: 那颗星球的内容远不止这些。你告诉卡塔利娜，自己如何深入米瑞利恩地底探险，在那里发现又一群人，甚至见到了被他们称作女王的人。她只是摇头，仿佛你所讲的某些事情实在令人难以置信。
rows.raw: "\n\nThere’s even more to the planet than that. You tell Catalina about your adventures delving into the depths of Myrellion, and finding yet another group of people down there, even meeting the one they called their queen. She just shakes her head, like she can hardly believe some of the stuff you’re telling her. "

rows.original: You’re sure there’s more to Myrellion than that, you tell her, but you’re still exploring that planet, and haven’t decided to move on yet.
rows.translation: 你告诉她，米瑞利恩肯定还有更多东西，不过自己仍在探索那颗星球，暂时还没有决定继续前进。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou’re sure there’s more to Myrellion than that, you tell her, but you’re still exploring that planet, and haven’t decided to move on yet. "

rows.original: “So you’ve seen two different kinds of insect people,” Catalina says, counting off on her fingers, “one planet that was in two parts, and a whole bunch more just plain weird shit,” she finishes. “How you gonna top that?” How about a planet that was blown up before you even got there? Catalina’s ears stand straight up. “Okay, you got me,” she says. You tell her about Zhèng Shi, or at least the asteroids that have that name, since they’re all that’s left of the Rush planet that was supposed to be there. The whole place was taken over by space pirates, and you had to fight your way through it, dealing with all kinds of people who called the lawless place home. Just being able to land almost got you shot down, and it didn’t get any less dangerous once you were there. “Okay, that’s a different kind of scary,” Catalina says with a shudder. “I don’t know how you have the guts to deal with that. I know everyone loves stories about space pirates, but I’d lose my shit if I actually had to deal with them.” She wraps her arms around herself, like she’s trying to fend off shivers. “I can only imagine ending up as someone’s breeding slave, or just getting gutted for parts.”
rows.translation: “所以你已经见过两种不同的昆虫人，”卡塔利娜一边说一边掰着手指数，“一颗分成两半的星球，还有一大堆纯粹古怪的破事，”她数完了。“你还能怎么超越这些？” 那如果是一颗在你抵达前就已经被炸碎的星球呢？ 卡塔利娜的耳朵笔直竖起。“好吧，算你厉害，”她说。 你向她讲起郑氏——或者至少是那些以郑氏为名的小行星，因为原本应该在那里的大淘金星球只剩下了它们。整片地区都被太空海盗占领，而你不得不一路杀出血路，应付各种把这片法外之地称作家园的人。光是成功着陆就差点让你被击落；真正抵达后，危险也丝毫没有减轻。 “好吧，这是另一种吓人，”卡塔利娜打着寒颤说道。“我不知道你哪来的胆量应付这些。我知道大家都爱听太空海盗的故事，但如果真要和他们打交道，我肯定会吓疯。”她用双臂抱住自己，像是想抵御寒意。“我只能想象自己最后沦为某个人的生育奴隶，或者干脆被开膛取走零件。”

rows.original: It was pretty bad, and you did have to deal with some heavily armed pirates, but you managed to learn your way around the place and not just survive but stand up against some of that place’s worst people before heading off to your next destination.
rows.translation: 情况确实相当糟糕，你也确实得对付一些全副武装的海盗；不过你还是摸清了那里的门路，不但存活下来，还挺身对抗了当地部分最恶劣的人，随后才前往下一处目的地。
rows.raw: "\n\nIt was pretty bad, and you did have to deal with some heavily armed pirates, but you managed to learn your way around the place and not just survive but stand up against some of that place’s worst people before heading off to your next destination. "

rows.original: It is pretty bad, but you’ve learned how to handle the place, and you’re still exploring it before it’s time to move on to your next destination.
rows.translation: 那里确实相当糟糕，但你已经学会该如何应付；在前往下一处目的地之前，你仍在继续探索。
rows.raw: "\n\nIt is pretty bad, but you’ve learned how to handle the place, and you’re still exploring it before it’s time to move on to your next destination. "

rows.original: “So your next stop was safer, right?” Catalina asks. “I’m not sure how it could be worse, but you’ve told me some pretty strange shit so far.” You tell her about your first approach to Dhaal, and how the tidally locked planet only has a small inhabitable zone, with one half unrelentingly hot and the other covered in ice. Catalina’s eyes widen, and she nods. “I’ve heard of places like that,” she says, “back when I was in college. I didn’t know any of the Rush planets were that way, though. What’s it like in the places you can actually go?” You describe the city running through the inhabitable zone, higher-tech than most of the Rush worlds but with severe divides between those who have money and connections and those who don’t. But it’s when you describe the natives of Dhaal that Catalina just starts staring at you, her mouth hanging open. “You have got to be shitting me.” She blinks a few times, like she’s still processing what the zaika must be like. “So they’ve got boobs like the kui-tan have balls, and they keep growing, but their junk is... in their tails? And the tail’s a dick and a pussy at the same time?” Her mouth moves, but no words come out, like she’s not sure what to say, until she settles on “What the actual fuck is that place?”
rows.translation: “那么下一站安全一点，对吧？”卡塔利娜问道。“我想不出还能怎么更糟，不过你到现在已经讲了一些相当古怪的破事。” 你告诉她，自己最初如何接近达尔；那颗被潮汐锁定的星球只有一小片宜居带，一半永远炽热，另一半则被冰层覆盖。卡塔利娜睁大眼睛，点点头。 “我听说过这样的地方，”她说，“大学时听说的。不过我不知道大淘金星球里也有这种地方。真正能去的区域是什么样？” 你描述了那座贯穿宜居带的城市；当地科技比大多数大淘金世界更先进，但有钱有关系的人与一无所有的人之间存在着严重鸿沟。然而，当你描述达尔的原住民时，卡塔利娜只是瞪着你，嘴巴张得老大。 “你他妈肯定在耍我。”她眨了好几次眼，仿佛仍在消化扎伊卡究竟是什么样。“所以她们的乳房就像奎坦人的睾丸一样，而且还会一直生长，但她们的性器官却...长在尾巴里？而且那条尾巴同时是肉棒和阴部？”她嘴唇开合，却发不出声音，似乎完全不知道该说什么；最后只憋出一句：“那地方到底是什么鬼？”

rows.original: It gets weirder, you tell her. You had quite the adventure involving the higher echelons of zaika society, dealing with the Zaibatsu who struggle for control over the city. After that, it was time to move on.
rows.translation: 你告诉她，事情还要更加古怪。你经历了一场牵涉扎伊卡社会上层的惊险事件，与争夺城市控制权的财阀打交道。之后，便到了继续前进的时候。
rows.raw: "\n\nIt gets weirder, you tell her. You had quite the adventure involving the higher echelons of zaika society, dealing with the Zaibatsu who struggle for control over the city. After that, it was time to move on. "

rows.original: It’s one hell of a place, to be sure, and you’re still exploring it, not quite ready to move on to wherever your next destination is.
rows.translation: 那里确实是个不得了的地方；你仍在继续探索，还没准备好前往下一处目的地。
rows.raw: "\n\nIt’s one hell of a place, to be sure, and you’re still exploring it, not quite ready to move on to wherever your next destination is. "

rows.original: Catalina just shakes her head, though she’s laughing a little. “Okay, keep going,” she says. “I know I’ll read about all these weird-ass places someday, but I can’t even imagine what you’re gonna tell me next. Where else have you been?” You tell her about Phaedra II, a radioactive wasteland that used to have thriving civilizations on it but was devastated by war before it became part of the Planet Rush. She frowns as you describe the irradiated lands and the bizarre creatures that roam there, but she also starts scribbling down sketches on her tablet again, like what you’ve said is inspiring her to create some new art. “Keep going, [pc.name],” she says after a moment. “This is like something out of a fever dream, but after everything else you’ve told me, I actually believe you. It’s like, if you were making this up, it’d be less strange.” As Catalina draws, you tell her about the people of Phaedra II, from the tentacle-headed nuka to the feline hyraxi and even the enormous behemoths, roaming the wastelands of the radioactive planet. She checks your descriptions against her sketches a few times, to make sure she’s getting everything right. “That’s a hell of a thing,” she mutters as she finishes up another quick sketch. “You still working your way across that one, or did you stop because you knew you couldn’t top it?” She sticks her tongue out at you a little.
rows.translation: 卡塔利娜只是摇头，不过也轻轻笑了。“好吧，继续，”她说。“我知道自己总有一天会读到所有这些怪地方，但我甚至想象不出你接下来会告诉我什么。你还去过哪里？” 你向她讲起菲德拉二号。那片放射性荒原曾孕育繁荣文明，却在成为星球大淘金的一部分以前就被战争摧毁。听你描述受辐射污染的土地与游荡其中的怪异生物时，她皱起眉头；不过，她也再次开始在平板上勾画草图，仿佛你的讲述给了她创作新作品的灵感。 “继续说，[pc.name]，”过了一会儿，她说道。“这听起来就像高烧时做的梦，但在你告诉我其他一切之后，我竟然真的相信你。如果这些是你编出来的，反而不会这么古怪。” 卡塔利娜绘画时，你向她讲述菲德拉二号的居民：从头生触手的努卡，到猫科的海拉克西，甚至还有游荡于放射性荒原的巨大贝希摩斯。她几次把你的描述与草图进行核对，确保一切都画得准确。 “真是不得了，”完成另一幅速写时，她低声说道。“你还在一步步探索那颗星球，还是因为知道不可能超越它，所以就停下了？”她朝你略微吐了吐舌头。

rows.original: You tell her that she probably wouldn’t believe what you had to go through on Phaedra II, as you can hardly believe it yourself even though it’s over. But that’s the last planet you’ve visited, and you might be done with the Planet Rush.
rows.translation: 你告诉她，她大概不会相信自己在菲德拉二号经历了什么；尽管一切已经结束，就连你自己都难以相信。不过，那是你造访的最后一颗星球，而你的星球大淘金之旅或许已经结束。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou tell her that she probably wouldn’t believe what you had to go through on Phaedra II, as you can hardly believe it yourself even though it’s over. But that’s the last planet you’ve visited, and you might be done with the Planet Rush. "

rows.original: You tell her that you’re still exploring Phaedra II, and you’re not sure where you’ll head once you’re done there, but you’ve got time to figure things out once that happens.
rows.translation: 你告诉她，自己仍在探索菲德拉二号；你还不知道完成那里的旅程后会去哪里，不过等那一天到来时，还有时间慢慢想清楚。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou tell her that you’re still exploring Phaedra II, and you’re not sure where you’ll head once you’re done there, but you’ve got time to figure things out once that happens. "

rows.original: Once your tale is finished, Catalina nods slowly, like she’s taking everything in. “Y’know, I can get why you’re doing the Rusher thing,” she says. “It’s a hundred percent not the life for me, but if I had the training and the guts, I might be out there too.” She laughs after a moment. “Yeah, right, like I could handle that... But no, tell me about your adventures some more next time you’re here.” She gestures at the shop’s painted walls. “Ain’t like I get out of Tavros much these days, so it’s good to hear about the rest of the galaxy.”
rows.translation: 你的故事讲完后，卡塔利娜缓缓点头，仿佛正在消化一切。“你知道，我能理解你为什么要当大淘金者，”她说。“这种生活百分之百不适合我，但如果我受过训练，也有那份胆量，说不定同样会去外面闯荡。”片刻后，她笑起来。“是啊，说得像我真应付得来似的...不过不是开玩笑，下次你来时，再多给我讲点冒险经历。”她朝店内彩绘的墙壁示意。“如今我几乎没机会离开塔弗罗斯，所以能听听银河系其他地方的事情也很好。”

rows.raw: "The Rush"

rows.translation: 大淘金
rows.raw: "The Rush"

rows.original: Tell her about your time in the Planet Rush.
rows.translation: 告诉她你参与星球大淘金的经历。
rows.raw: "Tell her about your time in the Planet Rush."

rows.original: Tattoos
rows.translation: 纹身
rows.raw: "Tattoos"

rows.original: You ask Catalina how she got into tattooing, and how long she’s been a tattoo artist. Her brown eyes light up, and she leans forward over the counter, with the air of someone who’s just been asked about their favorite subject. “Okay, so,” she begins, then giggles. “This might take a while.” You’ve got time. “So, I’ve been drawing since I was a little kid,” Catalina says. “That and sports were the only things that got me through school. And this one teacher I had who was, like, more excited about math than anyone should be, but that’s different.” She waves her hand like she’s brushing the subject change away. “I wanted to be an artist when I was a kid, but it was also like, how am I gonna make that work? Lots of people make art, but there’s not always steady money in that, and my moms were set on me making sure I had a job that paid.” You can understand that, which is about all you can say without getting into your own past. But you still had to take up a trade and work for your credits. “I figured I was shit out of luck after a while, because while I’ve always been good, I was never spectacular, y’know? Never fancy art school material or the kind of person that makes everyone go wow, I love your stuff, please take all of my credits. But when one of my friends saw this monster I was drawing and was like, that would make a kick-ass tattoo, it hit me, that was what I could do. rows.translation: 你询问卡塔利娜是怎样开始从事纹身工作的，以及她当纹身师有多久了。 她的棕色眼睛亮了起来，隔着柜台向前倾身，活像刚有人问起她最喜欢的话题。“好吧，事情是这样，”她开口说道，随后咯咯一笑。“这可能要讲一阵子。” 你有的是时间。 “我从很小的时候就一直画画，”卡塔利娜说道。“画画和体育是唯一帮我熬过学校生活的东西。还有一位教过我的老师；他对数学的热情高得有点不正常，不过那是另一回事。”她挥挥手，像要把跑题的内容扫到一边。“小时候我想成为艺术家，但同时又会想，要怎么才能靠它生活？很多人都创作艺术，可这行不一定有稳定收入；而妈妈们坚持要我确保自己有一份能赚钱的工作。” 你能理解这一点；如果不想谈及自己的过去，差不多也只能这么说。不过，你同样不得不学一门手艺，靠工作赚取信用点。 “过了一段时间，我觉得自己彻底没戏了；虽然我的水平一直不错，却从来没有出类拔萃，懂吧？我既不是读高端艺术学校的料，也不是那种能让所有人高喊‘哇，我好喜欢你的作品，请收下我全部信用点’的人。但有一次，一个朋友看见我画的怪物，说那东西拿来做纹身肯定帅炸了。那一刻我突然明白，这就是自己能做的事。于是我开始弄清楚该怎样入行。” 她指向髋部的豹纹斑点纹身；它们在运动短裤上沿清晰可见。“这两个是我最先纹的，出自教我纹身的那个人之手，”她说道。“我想要某种简单却又有点野性的图案。整个大学期间，我都在那个人手下工作；他的店就在学校附近。等我毕业时，基本已经准备好独自干这一行了。” 那么，最初那段日子是什么样？她亲手做的第一个纹身又是什么？ 卡塔利娜皱起脸，难为情地移开视线。“第一次给别人纹身时，我他妈紧张死了，”她说完摇摇头。“那是一家老派店铺，不是我在这里使用的纳米科技。”她朝店铺中央的机器示意。“我不知道他为什么坚持那种做法，也许他喜欢纹身真正永久，或者基本永久。随便吧。我的第一位客人是个高大的奥萨男人，全身上下纹得密密麻麻；我以前在店里见过他几次，所以他知道我仍在学习。但当他问店主我是否已经准备好时，店主说我没问题，于是...于是给他纹身时，我几乎用上了自己知道的每一种放松技巧，才没让双手颤抖。”她缓缓呼出一口气。“不过最后效果很好，他非常满意。” 图案是什么？ “一个长着超级大屁股的凯斯瑞特女孩，”卡塔利娜说完笑了起来。“他左肩胛骨上已经纹了一个长着超级巨乳的女孩，所以想再来一个与之平衡。”她又摇摇头，咯咯笑着。“从那以后，我纹过很多屁股，不过我觉得那依然是自己画过的最大屁股。” 所以，当时用的是老式纹身工具和真正的墨水。那么这里的机器呢？它是怎样工作的？ “噢，这东西酷极了，”她说道，双眼再次亮起。她轻点柜台上的平板。“我先在这里画图，然后机器会扫描你想纹的部位，这样开始之前就能看到最终效果。这让很多人非常开心；得知纹出来会是什么样后，他们兴奋得简直令你难以置信。不过，只要你满意图画和位置，我就把机器的纳米注射装置摆到位，然后它便开始工作。” 卡塔利娜咧嘴笑着，眼带自豪地望向店铺中央的机器。“最棒的是，它比老派纹身快得多。有些客人想纹大幅图案，最长也许只需要一个小时。我刚开业不久时，有个人来这里想纹覆盖整个后背的图案。最后画图花的时间比真正纹上去还长。” 她在自己身上测试过吗？ “噢，那当然，”卡塔利娜说道，并严肃地看了你一眼；那副表情出现在她生动的脸上，显得极不协调。“这就像行业法则，任何没在自己身上测试过的东西，都不能拿来给客人用。否则就像相信素食主义者会替你做好牛排。” 她转身向你展示左肩。那里纹着某种图案，不过看起来只像一堆带有荒谬数量锐角的线条，你完全看不懂它本该表示什么。“你听说过泰坦杀手吗？他们是

Worked real damn good.” You can tell, even if you have no idea what the logo is supposed to be. But if it hadn’t worked, would she have been able to remove it? “Yeah, that’s the best thing about the nanotech ink,” she says. “Goes in quick and easy, comes out the same way. It sounds like she’s doing well for herself in here. Catalina shrugs. “Can’t complain too much. Could be doing better, but could always be doing a lot worse, know what I mean?”

rows.original: You tell Catalina you want to get a tattoo. She lets out a cackle, and spins her stylus between her fingers, an eager smile on her face. “All right, we love a first-timer,” she says, then taps at her tablet, making screens swap rapidly across its surface. “Important part first, and I don’t mean what I’m gonna ink: getting inked will run you a thousand credits, no matter what you’re getting done or where.” She gestures with one hand, and rolls her eyes a little. “It’s a whole thing. I’ve got to set a flat rate, or I could get accused of discrimination by charging someone more because they’re getting an entire taur flank done or they want real intricate lines on their scales. Whole bunch of shit I don’t want to deal with. You got enough creds to cover that?”

rows.original: You tell her that you’re running a little low on credits. Catalina nods, then sets aside her stylus, resting her hands on the counter next to her tablet. “No problem, just come on back when you’ve got the money,” she says, though she sounds sympathetic. “And start thinking about what you want to get done.” She gives you a smile that’s just a little too practiced and professional. “Hope next time you come in, you’ve got the credits and something awesome for me to draw.”
rows.translation: 你告诉她，自己手头的信用点有点紧张。卡塔利娜点点头，随后放下触控笔，把双手搁在平板旁的柜台上。 “没问题，等有钱时再来就好，”她说道，语气中却透着同情。“也可以开始想想自己想纹什么。”她朝你露出一个稍显过度熟练、职业化的笑容。“希望你下次来时既带够信用点，也带来某个超棒的图案让我画。”

rows.original: You do have enough credits, so everything’s good there. Does she get a lot of people who come in trying to get something for free? “All the damn time,” Catalina says, rolling her eyes. “I’ve heard so many drunk sob stories from people who ‘have to get inked right now, because they just have to.’” She draws out the words, making them sound agonized, then laughs. “But since you’re not doing that, let’s talk about getting you some ink.” With another tap from Catalina’s stylus, the screens behind her counter switch to displays of the machine that’s standing in the middle of the tattoo shop, surrounded by example tattoos on different skin types, including scales and fur. “So, let me go through how this whole thing works before we get started, so you know what you’re getting into. It’s mostly simple and like a hundred percent safe, but there’s a bunch of stuff to go over.” Catalina clears her throat, assuming a much more businesslike stance instead of her usual casual pose. “So, the main thing is that the tattoo comes from tiny nanobots that the machine’s gonna inject under your skin,” she begins. “They’re mostly inert, and all they do is color the skin right above them and whatever’s coming out of it. That’s why they work on fur and scales, and not just skin like mine.” She pauses. “The bad part is that this doesn’t work on feathers, because the base of the feathers is too far from the rest of them. So all you get is this patch of colored feathers, and you can do that with dye.” Another tap of her stylus, and the screens change to show the machine in use. The scanner at the top comes down on a long, flexible cord, and positions itself above an arm with pale skin. “I’ll draw what you want, and once you’re good with the design, I send it into the machine. It’ll scan wherever you’re getting inked, so I hope you’re not shy about getting a little exposed.” She grins. “Once the scan’s done, I can show you what the tattoo will look like when it’s on. We can still make changes, but once you’re good with what’s on the screen, I get started and you get inked.” The screens’ display changes one more time, showing the scanner positioned over the pale arm, with dozens of tendrils coming down around it. The tendrils place themselves all along the person’s arm, and start to quiver, their tips barely touching the skin. When they move away, the first lines of a tattoo are left behind, long dark lines that slowly form a picture. “And that’s pretty much it,” Catalina says, looking at you. “Most people don’t have a reaction to the nanotech, but I’ve got an emergency call button for the station’s medical service, so if something goes horribly wrong I can get someone here real quick.” Her usual smile looks a little strained around the edges. “There is so much legal bullshit around running this place, I swear, but I’d also be so fucked if someone had a seizure on my table, so it’s worth it.” Are there any other issues you should worry about? You have some nanotech of your own in your system, and it would cause problems if the tattoo microsurgeons interfered with that. “Oh, no worries there,” Catalina says. “Like I said, these things are mostly inert, they just do a pigment change. There’s nothing in them that should, like, trigger any kind of immune reaction, and nobody’s found a species that’s got problems with them yet.” She looks a little tense for a moment. “But I am gonna limit you to one tattoo at a time, just to make sure. You good with that?” That’s fine. If nothing goes wrong, you can always get more. Anything else? “Couple policy bits,” she says, then holds up one finger. “First, if you’ve got any symbiotic or parasitic organisms on you, I won’t tattoo those, because those things are basically animals and can’t give informed consent.” She gives you a stern look. “Yes, I’m serious, and yes, people argue with me about this. Second,” Catalina continues, raising another finger, “You need your tattoo removed, I’ll do it for free, no questions asked.” That seems unusual. Why is that? She drops her hand and heaves a sigh. “I read about some obscure as fuck lawsuit when I was getting this place set up. Turns out, someone got a tattoo a couple days before a job interview and couldn’t afford to get it removed, and they sued the artist because the tattoo kept them from getting the job. I don’t know how the hell it worked that way, but I’m not taking a chance on losing this place thanks to some sue-happy jackass. So I’ll take out the microsurgeons for free. But it takes like ten minutes, so it’s not like it cuts into my day when it happens.” She shrugs. “Any other questions?” It sounds like she’s covered everything. “Sweet.” Catalina leans forward over the counter, making her boobs bounce a little in the heavy sports bra holding them in place. “So, you ready to get inked?”
rows.translation: 你确实带够了信用点，所以这方面一切正常。是否经常有人进来，试图白拿东西？ “他妈一直都有，”卡塔利娜翻着白眼说道。“我已经听过太多醉鬼的悲惨故事；他们‘必须现在立刻纹身，因为就是非纹不可。’”她拖长每个字，让语气听起来痛苦万分，随后笑了起来。“不过既然你不是来干这个的，我们就谈谈给你添些墨吧。” 卡塔利娜再次轻点触控笔，柜台后方的屏幕随即切换，显示出纹身店中央那台机器；周围还陈列着各种不同皮肤类型的纹身范例，其中包括鳞片和毛皮。“那么，开始之前，我先说明整套流程是怎样运作的，好让你知道自己要面对什么。大体很简单，也可以说百分之百安全，不过有一大堆东西必须讲清楚。” 卡塔利娜清了清嗓子，不再保持平时随意的姿态，而是摆出更加职业化的架势。“首先，最主要的一点：纹身来自机器注射到皮肤下的微型纳米机器人，”她开始解释。“它们基本处于惰性状态，唯一的作用就是改变正上方皮肤以及从中长出之物的颜色。所以，它们不只适用于像我这样的皮肤，也能在毛皮和鳞片上发挥作用。”她顿了顿。“坏处是，这对羽毛无效，因为羽毛根部距离其他部分太远。最后只能得到一片变色羽毛，而这种效果用染料就能做到。” 她又轻点一下触控笔，屏幕切换为机器使用时的画面。顶部扫描仪沿着一根柔性长线缆降下，停在一条皮肤白皙的手臂上方。“我会画出你想要的东西；等你满意图案后，我就把它传入机器。机器会扫描你想纹身的地方，所以希望你不会介意稍微露出一点身体。”她咧嘴一笑。“扫描完成后，我可以向你展示纹身真正落在身上时的样子。之后依然能修改；不过等你满意屏幕上的效果，我就开始操作，你也会得到纹身。” 屏幕画面再次改变：扫描仪停在那条白皙手臂上方，周围垂下数十根卷须。卷须沿着那人的手臂各处排列，开始轻轻颤动，尖端几乎贴上皮肤。它们移开时，纹身最初的线条已经留在原地；一道道深色长线缓缓组成图像。 “差不多就是这样，”卡塔利娜看着你说道。“大多数人不会对纳米科技产生不良反应，不过我这里有一个连接空间站医疗服务的紧急呼叫按钮；万一出了极其严重的问题，我能很快叫人过来。”她平常的笑容边缘显得略微僵硬。“我发誓，经营这地方牵涉的法律废话多得要命；不过，要是有人在我的工作台上癫痫发作，我也会彻底完蛋，所以这些措施值得。” 还有没有其他需要担心的问题？你体内有自己的纳米科技；如果纹身微型外科机器人对其造成干扰，便会带来麻烦。 “噢，不用担心，”卡塔利娜说道。“就像我说的，这些东西基本处于惰性状态，只会改变色素。里面没有任何东西应该会，那个，引发某种免疫反应；而且到现在还没有发现哪个种族会和它们产生问题。”片刻间，她看起来有点紧张。“不过，为了保险起见，我一次只会给你纹一个。能接受吗？” 没问题。如果一切正常，以后随时能纹更多。还有别的吗？ “还有几项政策规定，”她说着举起一根手指。“第一，如果你身上带有共生或寄生生物，我不会给那些东西纹身，因为它们基本上是动物，无法作出知情同意。”她严肃地看了你一眼。“没错，我是认真的；也没错，确实有人为此和我争论。第二，”卡塔利娜继续说道，又举起一根手指，“如果需要去除纹身，我会免费处理，什么都不问。” 这似乎很不寻常。为什么？ 她放下手，重重叹了口气。“筹备这家店时，我读到一桩他妈极其冷门的诉讼。原来，有个人在求职面试前几天纹了身，却付不起去除费用；因为纹身害他没拿到工作，所以他把纹身师告了。我不知道事情到底怎么会变成那样，不过，我可不想因为某个动不动就起诉的混蛋而冒着失去这家店的风险。所以，我会免费取出微型外科机器人。反正只需要十分钟左右，真有人来处理时，也不会怎么占用我的一天。”她耸耸肩。“还有其他问题吗？” 听起来她已经把一切都讲清楚了。 “很好。”卡塔利娜隔着柜台向前倾身，让结实运动胸罩固定着的乳房微微弹跳。“那么，准备好纹身了吗？”

rows.original: You tell Catalina that you want to have one of your tattoos removed. She nods quickly, and gestures toward the tattoo chair and table. “Gotcha, [pc.name],” she says. “Let’s get you taken care of, this won’t take long.” You make yourself comfortable as Catalina prepares the machine. After a moment, she looks you over, like she’s trying to remember what she’s put on you and where. “So, what’re we de-inking today?”

rows.raw: "It’s a pleasure to meet you ladies."

rows.original: I have to say...” You pause for dramatic effect, curling your [pc.lips] into a devious smile and putting on your best suave voice. “I’m looking forward to what sort of trouble you gals might be.
rows.translation: 不得不说...”你故意停顿，[pc.lips]勾起狡黠笑容，用最潇洒的嗓音说道：“我很期待看看今晚能和你们惹出什么麻烦。
rows.raw: "I have to say...” You pause for dramatic effect, curling your [pc.lips] into a devious smile and putting on your best suave voice. “I’m looking forward to what sort of trouble you gals might be."

rows.original: Lookin’ forward to hanging with you gals for the night.
rows.translation: 我很期待今晚和你们一起玩。
rows.raw: "Lookin’ forward to hanging with you gals for the night."

rows.original: The three talkative girls all immediately light up upon hearing your name, with Fisianna giving a small twitch of her ears, but otherwise still unmoving.
rows.translation: 听到你的名字，三个健谈的女孩立刻双眼放光；菲希安娜的耳朵轻轻一颤，除此之外仍一动不动。
rows.raw: "\n\nThe three talkative girls all immediately light up upon hearing your name, with Fisianna giving a small twitch of her ears, but otherwise still unmoving. "

rows.original: “No fuckin’ way! You’re the [pc.name] Steele?! Now you’re just tryin’ too hard to impre-OW!” Tarariel manages to blurt out before being sharply ribbed by Aya. The harpy-morph quickly clears her throat after giving Tarariel another one of her death stares.
rows.translation: “不会吧！你就是那个[pc.name]·斯蒂尔？！你现在也太想给人留下印——嗷！”塔拉瑞尔脱口而出，却被阿雅猛地用手肘顶了一下。鹰身女孩狠狠瞪了她一眼。
rows.raw: "\n\n“No fuckin’ way! You’re the [pc.name] Steele?! Now you’re just tryin’ too hard to impre-OW!” Tarariel manages to blurt out before being sharply ribbed by Aya. The harpy-morph quickly clears her throat after giving Tarariel another one of her death stares."

rows.original: “What she meant to say was, it’s nice to meet a multi-billionaire magnate’s
rows.translation: “她真正想说的是，能在这么遥远的地方见到一位亿万富豪巨头的
rows.raw: "\n\n“What she meant to say was, it’s nice to meet a multi-billionaire magnate’s "

rows.original: son
rows.translation: 儿子
rows.raw: "son"

rows.original: daughter
rows.translation: 女儿
rows.raw: "daughter"

rows.original: and heir to his company all the way over here... in a seedy bar no less!”
rows.translation: 和公司继承人真是太好了...更别说还是在这种乌烟瘴气的酒吧里！”
rows.raw: " and heir to his company all the way over here... in a seedy bar no less!” "

rows.original: Aya looks visibly embarrassed having put that fact to light now. “So what does bring someone like you to this place?” She repeats. “I wouldn’t have thought someone of your import would be here instead of chasing after your fortune.”
rows.translation: 阿雅把这件事说破后明显有些尴尬。“所以，像你这样的人到底为什么会来这里？”她再次问道。“我还以为你这种人会去更高档的地方。”
rows.raw: "\n\nAya looks visibly embarrassed having put that fact to light now. “So what does bring someone like you to this place?” She repeats. “I wouldn’t have thought someone of your import would be here instead of chasing after your fortune.”"

rows.original: <i>“Well, I’m not heir to the Steele Tech company yet anyways. I’m working on that currently.
rows.translation: <i>“嗯，我现在还不是斯蒂尔科技公司的继承人。我正在为此努力。
rows.raw: "\n\n<i>“Well, I’m not heir to the Steele Tech company yet anyways. I’m working on that currently. "

rows.original: Also, it doesn’t hurt to have a moment of reprieve every once in awhile in between traversing planets on this big planetary Rush, especially in the company of such lovely gals.
rows.translation: 而且，在这场横跨各个星球的浩大星球淘金热中，偶尔偷闲喘口气也没什么不好，尤其还有这么可爱的姑娘们相伴。
rows.raw: "Also, it doesn’t hurt to have a moment of reprieve every once in awhile in between traversing planets on this big planetary Rush, especially in the company of such lovely gals."

rows.original: Also, it doesn’t hurt to have a moment of reprieve every once in awhile in between traversing planets on this big planetary Rush, especially with such an interesting group of ladies.
rows.translation: 而且，在这场横跨各个星球的浩大星球淘金热中，偶尔偷闲喘口气也没什么不好，尤其还能和你们这样有趣的一群女士作伴。
rows.raw: "Also, it doesn’t hurt to have a moment of reprieve every once in awhile in between traversing planets on this big planetary Rush, especially with such an interesting group of ladies."

rows.original: Also, it doesn’t hurt to have a moment of respite every once in awhile in-between traversing planets on this big planetary Rush, especially with a bunch of... unique women like yourselves.
rows.translation: 而且，在这场横跨各个星球的浩大星球淘金热中，偶尔休息片刻也没什么不好，尤其身边还有你们这样...独特的女性。
rows.raw: "Also, it doesn’t hurt to have a moment of respite every once in awhile in-between traversing planets on this big planetary Rush, especially with a bunch of... unique women like yourselves."

rows.original: Aya and Tarariel both lean their heads in towards each other, whispering to one another in fevered tones, though with the noise of the bar around you, you can’t discern what they’re talking about. Britannia squeezes your shoulder again before turning her attention towards Fisianna who, now that you look at her, has her gaze set squarely on you in a trance-like state. For the first time, you are able to see her visage in the dim light of the bar. She has a cute and very feminine face, despite not having much makeup on as far as you can tell. She has long eyelashes that shadow her bright golden feline eyes that you could become lost in almost as much as she seems lost in staring at you. You also notice that she has furred arms tipped with paws, which isn’t something you normally would see on a kaithrit. It seems she has more in common with the group of girls than she initially let on.
rows.translation: 阿雅和塔拉瑞尔把脑袋凑在一起，热切地低声交谈；酒吧周围太过嘈杂，你听不清她们在说什么。布里塔妮娅则饶有兴趣地盯着你，尾巴在座位后缓缓摆动。菲希安娜依旧沉默，不过你能感觉到她偶尔会偷偷看你。
rows.raw: "\n\nAya and Tarariel both lean their heads in towards each other, whispering to one another in fevered tones, though with the noise of the bar around you, you can’t discern what they’re talking about. Britannia squeezes your shoulder again before turning her attention towards Fisianna who, now that you look at her, has her gaze set squarely on you in a trance-like state. For the first time, you are able to see her visage in the dim light of the bar. She has a cute and very feminine face, despite not having much makeup on as far as you can tell. She has long eyelashes that shadow her bright golden feline eyes that you could become lost in almost as much as she seems lost in staring at you. You also notice that she has furred arms tipped with paws, which isn’t something you normally would see on a kaithrit. It seems she has more in common with the group of girls than she initially let on."

rows.original: Britannia apparently notices that Fisianna is staring hard at you, too. “Yoohoo... wakey wakey.” The dragon woman gently coos as she waves her hand lightly in front of Fisianna’s view to grab her attention. The catgirl lets out a small yelp of surprise as she slightly jumps in her seat. Her cheeks start to turn pink from embarrassment and looks hurriedly down at her lap again. “Everything alright, kitten?” Britannia asks in a gentle, almost soothing manner.
rows.translation: 布里塔妮娅显然也注意到菲希安娜正紧盯着你。“喂喂...醒醒啦。”龙女轻声哄着，在菲希安娜面前轻轻挥手。猫娘猛地回过神，脸颊迅速涨红。“一切都好吗，小猫咪？”布里塔妮娅温柔地问道。
rows.raw: "\n\nBritannia apparently notices that Fisianna is staring hard at you, too. “Yoohoo... wakey wakey.” The dragon woman gently coos as she waves her hand lightly in front of Fisianna’s view to grab her attention. The catgirl lets out a small yelp of surprise as she slightly jumps in her seat. Her cheeks start to turn pink from embarrassment and looks hurriedly down at her lap again. “Everything alright, kitten?” Britannia asks in a gentle, almost soothing manner."

rows.original: “U-uhm... yeah. I’m o-ok. Just... I kind of, I mean, u-uh...” Fisianna babbles, struggling to find the right words until her cheeks start flowing a deeper red. “I need to go... to the bathroom I-I mean. Please excuse me.”
rows.translation: “呃、呃...是的。我没、没事。只是...我有点，我是说，呃...”菲希安娜结结巴巴，努力寻找合适措辞，双颊越来越红。“我得去...去洗手间，我、我是说。失陪一下。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“U-uhm... yeah. I’m o-ok. Just... I kind of, I mean, u-uh...” Fisianna babbles, struggling to find the right words until her cheeks start flowing a deeper red. “I need to go... to the bathroom I-I mean. Please excuse me.” "

rows.original: You and Britannia shift out of your seats to let Fisianna go on her way. The catgirl hurriedly stands up and walks past the both of you, not making eye contact. You can tell from a quick glance at her face that she looks on the verge of tears, possibly out of embarrassment from what you can surmise. You also notice that she does not seem to be heading directly towards the bar’s bathroom but rather an emergency side exit. Britannia moves to sit back down, but not before glancing at the door Fisianna went through and giving you a look of concern. You can choose to follow the feline to see what is wrong, or trust that she will come back to her friends once she is better.
rows.translation: 你和布里塔妮娅从座位上挪开，让菲希安娜出去。猫娘匆忙站起，从你们身旁走过，全程不敢与人对视。你只消瞥一眼她的脸，就看得出她几乎快哭出来了。她快步穿过酒吧，消失在人群中。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou and Britannia shift out of your seats to let Fisianna go on her way. The catgirl hurriedly stands up and walks past the both of you, not making eye contact. You can tell from a quick glance at her face that she looks on the verge of tears, possibly out of embarrassment from what you can surmise. You also notice that she does not seem to be heading directly towards the bar’s bathroom but rather an emergency side exit. Britannia moves to sit back down, but not before glancing at the door Fisianna went through and giving you a look of concern. You can choose to follow the feline to see what is wrong, or trust that she will come back to her friends once she is better. "

rows.original: You make your way towards the exotic girls again, eager to share some more stories with them. Britannia the dragoness scooches over to give you room to sit at the end of the booth and wraps a familiar arm around your shoulder when you sit down next to her.
rows.translation: 你再次走向那群异域女孩，迫不及待地想与她们分享更多故事。龙女布里塔妮娅往旁边挪了挪，让你能坐在卡座末端她的身边。
rows.raw: "You make your way towards the exotic girls again, eager to share some more stories with them. Britannia the dragoness scooches over to give you room to sit at the end of the booth and wraps a familiar arm around your shoulder when you sit down next to her."

rows.original: “[pc.name]! Good to see you again! I’ve been dying to get to know more about you!” Aya, the harpy-morph chirps giddily.
rows.translation: “[pc.name]！很高兴又见到你！我一直特别想更多了解你！”鹰身变形者阿雅兴奋地啁啾道。
rows.raw: "\n\n“[pc.name]! Good to see you again! I’ve been dying to get to know more about you!” Aya, the harpy-morph chirps giddily."

rows.original: Tarariel, the fiery-headed kitsune-morph next to her adopts a wolfish grin on her face. “Yeah, I bet you do! We know about ALL the things you wanna do t-mmm-mph!” Is all she can manage to say before the bird-girl brings a feathered hand to the fox-girl’s mouth, cutting her off.
rows.translation: 她旁边那名火红头发的狐妖变形者塔拉瑞尔露出狼一般的坏笑。“对啊，我敢说你当然想！我们可知道你想对——唔嗯！”阿雅一把捂住了她的嘴。
rows.raw: "\n\nTarariel, the fiery-headed kitsune-morph next to her adopts a wolfish grin on her face. “Yeah, I bet you do! We know about ALL the things you wanna do t-mmm-mph!” Is all she can manage to say before the bird-girl brings a feathered hand to the fox-girl’s mouth, cutting her off."

rows.original: Aya gives you a nervous laugh before blurting, “Just ignore her.”
rows.translation: 阿雅紧张地笑了笑，脱口说道：“别理她。”
rows.raw: "\n\nAya gives you a nervous laugh before blurting, “Just ignore her.”"

rows.original: You and Britannia laugh heartily at that. Soon, a waitress approaches your table so that you and the girls can order some drinks. She gives you an unsubtle wink before she sashays over to the bar. When she arrives with drinks in hand, she places them down on the table and leaves to serve other patrons. After taking a sip of your beverage, you start to swap stories between each other. In-between tales you look over towards Fisianna. She still seems as shy as can be, unmoving and unspeaking as the night wanes on. Britannia of course notices your wayward glances towards Fisianna and smiles reassuringly at you whenever she catches your eye.
rows.translation: 你和布里塔妮娅都开怀大笑。很快，一名女服务员来到桌边，让你和姑娘们点酒。她毫不掩饰地朝你眨眼，随后扭着臀部离去。酒水送来后，你们继续聊天，分享旅途中的故事和笑话。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou and Britannia laugh heartily at that. Soon, a waitress approaches your table so that you and the girls can order some drinks. She gives you an unsubtle wink before she sashays over to the bar. When she arrives with drinks in hand, she places them down on the table and leaves to serve other patrons. After taking a sip of your beverage, you start to swap stories between each other. In-between tales you look over towards Fisianna. She still seems as shy as can be, unmoving and unspeaking as the night wanes on. Britannia of course notices your wayward glances towards Fisianna and smiles reassuringly at you whenever she catches your eye."

rows.original: Between one particularly juicy story that you tell about a haywire computer you used which ran amok because of a virus it contracted from an elicit site, Britannia softly nudges Fisianna asking, “Hey, Kitten. Wanna share a little story to add to that? You’re pretty techy when it comes to that stuff!”
rows.translation: 你讲起一个格外精彩的故事：一台失控电脑因从非法网站感染病毒而到处作乱。布里塔妮娅轻轻碰了碰菲希安娜，说道：“嘿，小猫咪。想不想也分享个故事？你很懂这类技术吧！”
rows.raw: "\n\nBetween one particularly juicy story that you tell about a haywire computer you used which ran amok because of a virus it contracted from an elicit site, Britannia softly nudges Fisianna asking, “Hey, Kitten. Wanna share a little story to add to that? You’re pretty techy when it comes to that stuff!”"

rows.original: Fisianna shifts in her chair a bit, taking a small sip of her fizzy drink before murmuring, “U-uh... It’s ok. I actually... k-kind of need to use the bathroom... I-I drank too much.”
rows.translation: 菲希安娜在椅子上挪了挪，小口啜饮汽水，随后低声说道：“呃...我没事。其实...我、我有点想去洗手间...我、我喝得太多了。”
rows.raw: "\n\nFisianna shifts in her chair a bit, taking a small sip of her fizzy drink before murmuring, “U-uh... It’s ok. I actually... k-kind of need to use the bathroom... I-I drank too much.”"

rows.original: Fisianna’s drink actually looks barely touched by your observation. Britannia gives Fisianna a brief look of concern before ushering you to move and conceding to slide out of her seat to let Fisianna out of the booth.
rows.translation: 依你观察，菲希安娜的饮料其实几乎没动。布里塔妮娅担忧地看了她一眼，随后示意你挪动，并同意从座位里让出来。
rows.raw: "\n\nFisianna’s drink actually looks barely touched by your observation. Britannia gives Fisianna a brief look of concern before ushering you to move and conceding to slide out of her seat to let Fisianna out of the booth."

rows.original: “Yeah, go ahead.” Britannia says warily.
rows.translation: “好吧，去吧。”布里塔妮娅不放心地说道。
rows.raw: "\n\n“Yeah, go ahead.” Britannia says warily."

rows.original: Fisianna hurriedly stands up and walks past the both of you, not making eye contact.
rows.translation: 菲希安娜匆忙站起，从你们两人身旁走过，全程不敢与人对视。
rows.raw: "\n\nFisianna hurriedly stands up and walks past the both of you, not making eye contact. "

rows.original: You can tell from a quick glance at her face that she looks on the verge of tears, though you have a fairly good idea of why that is.
rows.translation: 你只消瞥一眼她的脸，就看得出她几乎快哭出来了，不过你大致知道原因。
rows.raw: "You can tell from a quick glance at her face that she looks on the verge of tears, though you have a fairly good idea of why that is. "

rows.original: You can tell from a quick glance at her face that she looks on the verge of tears.
rows.translation: 你只消瞥一眼她的脸，就看得出她几乎快哭出来了。
